criteria.criterion: `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` exposes a pure validation function that, given a structured answer plus the recorded REST evidence, returns an UNVERIFIED reason exactly when the answer reports an Epic field id as null AND the recorded field inventory holds zero `customfield_*` ids (or no usable field read at all), and returns "no problem" otherwise

`main()` calls it after the agent run: on an UNVERIFIED verdict it prints a `::error::` naming both 941b candidate causes plus the observed inventory, records the verdict in `run_metadata.json`, and returns a non-zero exit code — while still writing `capability_map.json` and `evidence.json`
`main()` behaviour is unchanged for every other answer shape (Epic fields present, or absent alongside other `customfield_*` ids): same exit code and same artifacts as before this change
no pre-create `await_required_fields` call is added anywhere (the 941b ban holds), and a test pins that `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` contains no such call site

unit tests drive the validator with: a system-only inventory + null Epic ids (UNVERIFIED), a provisioned inventory + null Epic ids (accepted — genuine degrade), populated Epic ids (accepted), and no field read captured (UNVERIFIED)

Bug 'Capability map declares Epic fields absent without validating the report against the recorded field inventory' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds
